slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slot.brief: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges: an electron and a proton (or same particle through two different potentials); compare de Broglie wavelengths using the ratio for equal KE vs equal momentum.

stem: An electron and a proton have equal kinetic energies. If their de Broglie wavelengths are $\lambda_e$ and $\lambda_p$, respectively, what is $\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}$?

verdicts.working: For equal kinetic energy, p = √(2mK) and λ = h/p. Therefore λₑ/λₚ = √(mₚ/mₑ).

working:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$
$\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_pK_p}{m_eK_e}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$

Independent check: For equal kinetic energy, p = √(2mK) and λ = h/p. Therefore λₑ/λₚ = √(mₚ/mₑ).
solution:
For a particle with kinetic energy $K$, the de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$. Since $K_e=K_p$,
$$\frac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\frac{m_pK_p}{m_eK_e}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_p}{m_e}}.$$
